story.head: The Stars are rolling
paras: The Predators won the teams’ first meeting this season, 2-1 in Nashville on Oct 3. The Stars are on a tear, five straight wins. The Predators (12-6-5) beat Pittsburgh 4-3 on Saturday. This is a Central Division matchup, with the Preds fourth (tied for 11th in the NHL) and the Stars second (tied for sixth). The Central has been the strongest of the four divisions so far.

The Predators’ record (.630) is running ahead of what their chances are worth (.535), largely thanks to pulling off wins in one-goal games. So is the Stars’ (.696 on chances worth .601), largely because they’re 9-4 in one-goal games.

The Predators keep things calm after the whistle (2nd lowest), play some of the league’s fastest games (3rd) and get pinned in their own end on long shifts (31st). The Stars, by contrast, play slow, tight games (lowest). They also block more shots than anyone (1st), but take more penalties than they draw (32nd). Dallas has allowed 2.35 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. The Stars keep shots away, but the Predators give up plenty.

Filip Forsberg (9 G / 16 A / 25 P in 23 GP) leads the Predators in scoring, and Steven Stamkos (12 G / 12 A / 24 P in 23 GP) has a team-high twelve goals. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (10 G / 18 A / 28 P in 23 GP) leads the way in scoring, with seven points in his last five games. Jason Robertson (10 G / 16 A / 26 P in 23 GP) is next in line.
Juuse Saros (8-4-4 / .916 SV% in 16 GS) has been terrific for Nashville and is expected to start. Jake Oettinger (13-4-1 / .909 SV% in 18 GS) is expected to go for Dallas.
